sections.section_name: Section A - Choose the Correct Answer

questions.question_text: Which unit is best to measure the weight of a heavy school bag?
How many total days are there in a standard leap year?
Which of these capital letters has a vertical line of symmetry?
If 1 litre equals 1000 millilitres, how many millilitres are in 3 litres?
Which month of the year has the least number of days?
6 equal groups of 4 apples each gives a total of how many apples?
If a movie starts at 4:00 PM and lasts for 2 hours, at what time does it end?
Which standard tool is commonly used to weigh vegetables at a shop?
What do we call a chart that organizes information using tally marks and numbers?
How many hours are there in one complete day?
A shopkeeper has 2 kg of sugar. He packs them into small packets of 500 g each. How many packets does he make? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Since 1 kg equals 1000 g, 2 kg equals 2000 g. Dividing 2000 g by 500 g, the shopkeeper makes exactly 4 small packets.

questions.question_text: If 3 children share 36 pencils equally among themselves, how many pencils does each child get? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: We divide 36 pencils by 3 children. Each child will receive 12 pencils because 3 multiplied by 12 equals 36.

questions.question_text: Does a butterfly have a line of symmetry? Explain briefly. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Yes, a butterfly has a line of symmetry down its exact center. Both its left and right wings match each other perfectly.

questions.question_text: A water bottle holds 750 mL of water. Renu drinks 250 mL from it. How much water is left inside? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: We subtract the drunk water (250 mL) from the total capacity (750 mL). There is exactly 500 mL of water left inside.

questions.question_text: How many days are there altogether in the months of January and February during a normal year? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: January has 31 days and a normal February has 28 days. Adding them together, there are 59 days altogether in both months.

questions.question_text: A school bus leaves the station at 8:15 AM and takes 45 minutes to reach the school. At what time does the bus reach the school? Show your steps. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: The bus starts at 8:15 AM. Adding 45 minutes to 15 minutes brings us to 9:00 AM exactly. Therefore, the bus reaches the school precisely at 9:00 AM after completing the journey.

questions.question_text: A fruit seller records the number of apples sold in four days: Monday 15, Tuesday 20, Wednesday 10, and Thursday 25. What is the total number of apples sold in these four days? [40-50 words]
questions.answer: To find the total, we add the sales of all four days: 15 plus 20 is 35, plus 10 is 45, and plus 25 gives 70. The fruit seller sold a total of 70 apples over these four days.

sections.section_name: Section D - Mathematical Expression & Data Analysis

questions.question_text: Look at a clock showing 3:00. Describe the positions of both hands, the type of angle they form, and calculate what time it will be after 3 hours and 30 minutes. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: At 3:00, the minute hand points at 12 and the hour hand points at 3, forming a right angle. Adding 3 hours to 3:00 gives 6:00, and adding 30 more minutes results in 6:30. Therefore, the time will be 6:30.

questions.question_text: A container has 5 litres and 400 mL of juice. If 2 litres and 100 mL of juice are poured out into glasses, how much juice is left in the container? Show complete steps. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: We arrange the quantities by litres and millilitres. Subtracting the millilitres, 400 mL minus 100 mL leaves 300 mL. Subtracting the litres, 5 litres minus 2 litres leaves 3 litres. Therefore, there is exactly 3 litres and 300 mL of juice left in the container.
